items.title: Tesla’s solar roof is dead. Here’s what went wrong

items.title: Waymo hands over documents in NHTSA’s child collision probe

items.title: Why is the DOJ investigating Andreessen Horowitz’s board seats?
items.summary: Andreessen Horowitz has two partners sitting on the boards of companies that now compete with each other: Ben Horowitz at Databricks and Martin Casado at Fivetran. Nothing too scandalous on the surface, except the Department of Justice has reportedly been investigating the arrangement for almost a year, dusting off a 112-year-old antitrust law that’s rarely…

items.title: US government lab is probing Chinese lidar for security vulnerabilities
items.summary: The security review is being performed by the Idaho National Laboratory, and the research is being funded by a company -- or a group of companies -- in the electric and autonomous vehicle industries.

items.title: Oura faces lawsuit accusing it of misleading consumers about sleep-tracking accuracy
items.summary: The lawsuit alleges that Oura rings are unable to measure any of the physiological signals needed to assess sleep quality or determine sleep stages.

items.title: Walmart to finally start accepting Apple Pay and Google Pay
items.summary: Are pigs flying? Walmart has finally caved on its refusal to support Apple Pay and Google Pay.

items.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
items.summary: There's about to be a big fight to secure access to space.

items.title: Tesla recalls 3 million cars as part of China-wide push to stop hidden door handles
items.summary: Tesla and eight other automakers will install warning labels that help occupants identify the often hard-to-find manual door releases.

items.title: Private equity firm Apollo confirms data breach amid hacking wave targeting financial giants
items.summary: The private equity giant confirms a breach, weeks after Google researchers said hackers were targeting financial companies.

items.title: Senator asks US government watchdog to review how feds use hacking tools
items.summary: Senator Ron Wyden sent a letter to the U.S. federal watchdog requesting a comprehensive review of how the FBI, DEA, ICE's HSI, and the Secret Service use hacking tools and spyware against Americans.

items.title: Tesla, Uber, and Waymo all get the OK to operate thousands of robotaxis in Nevada
items.summary: Together, these permits would allow up to 8,000 robotaxis to be deployed over the next 12 months.

items.title: AI data startup Micro1 reaches $500M gross run rate amid AI training boom
items.summary: Surging demand for AI training data is driving rapid growth for the startup and its rivals.

items.summary: Investors want founders who understand the financial reality of their business. Messy data, misunderstood metrics, or waiting until you’re nearly out of cash to start fundraising can cost founders leverage, valuation, and even a term sheet. items.title: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
items.summary: Businesses are willing to flop back and forth as each lab releases new models, volatility that should give both companies' investors pause about how "sticky" enterprise AI spending really is.

items.title: ChatGPT can now send texts for you with new Apple Messages plug-in
items.summary: Ever wanted someone else to do your texting for you? ChatGPT is being offered up as an automated text scribe via a new Apple Messages integration.

items.title: The Enhanced Games — tech’s steroid extravaganza — didn’t pay off, as company posts $60 million loss
items.summary: An effort to transform the world of sports through steroid use doesn't exactly seem to be bearing financial fruit.

items.title: OK, can we actually cool data centers with our pee?

items.title: Someone targeted security researchers using a fake crypto conference as a lure

items.title: Mark buys a castle
items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg just bought a cozy abode somewhat close to Meta’s international headquarters in Ireland.

items.title: Google gives publishers a new way to fight AI-driven traffic losses
items.summary: Google is giving publishers a new button that lets readers make them a preferred source across Search, Discover, and Google News, potentially boosting their traffic as AI search sends fewer clicks to the web.
